prompt.context_jp: 薄暗い読影室の一角で、機械の低い唸り___響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 機械の低い唸り___響いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle: 'Only the low hum of the machines echoed.'

feedback.correct_en: With 「だけ」 implied (only the hum), が marks the exhaustive subject — nothing else was heard but this. New information introducing the scene also favors が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would set the hum as a topic for contrast or comment, but here the sentence is simply presenting what existed in the silence.

contrast_examples.en: As for insect sounds, I don't hear them (topic/contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 広瀬裕乃___まだ入って日が浅く、ただ相槌を打ちながら耳を傾けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 広瀬裕乃___まだ入って日が浅く…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the sentence topic.

feedback.correct_en: Hirose is being established as the topic — the sentence then comments on her situation (newly joined, just nodding along). は fits topic-setting.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as new/exhaustive information, but she's being introduced as the theme of the sentence, not identified against alternatives.

prompt.context_jp: 扉が開き、白衣姿の甘春杏___まっすぐに悠木のデスクへ赴いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 白衣姿の甘春杏___まっすぐに悠木のデスクへ赴いた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Amakasu is appearing on scene as new information — the narrator reports her entrance. が marks this fresh appearance.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat her as an already-established topic, but this sentence is the moment of her entering the room.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアが開いて、彼女が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: The door opened and she came in (new).

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女は毎朝ここに来る。

prompt.context_jp: 「五十嵐___放射線技師です 医師ではありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 五十嵐___放射線技師です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Igarashi is the topic being described — his profession is stated. は fits X-wa Y-da identification/description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would answer 'who is the technician?' with exhaustive focus. Here Kaburaki is simply characterizing Igarashi.

contrast_examples.en: He is the doctor (identifying among others).

prompt.context_jp: 「読影して 診断を下しているの___甘春先生です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 診断を下しているの___甘春先生です。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: This is a cleft/identifying structure: 'The one who makes diagnoses IS Dr. Amakasu.' が marks exhaustive identification among possibilities.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a general topic comment and lose the pointed 'it is Amakasu, not Igarashi' force Omori needs here.

contrast_examples.en: The one who did it is me (exhaustive).
As for me, I did it (topic).

prompt.context_jp: 「患者の命___かかってるんだ 技師が余計な口を挟むな！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 患者の命___かかってるんだ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Kaburaki is asserting a fresh, forceful fact: 'A patient's life is on the line!' が emphasizes this as new, urgent information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would soften it into a general topic comment, losing the exclamatory urgency of the moment.

contrast_examples.en: As for time, there is none (calmer topic).

prompt.context_jp: 「生まれた時から この病院のお嬢様なんて 人生勝ち組もいいとこだよな」の流れで:「彼女___生まれた時から この病院のお嬢様だ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___生まれた時から この病院のお嬢様だ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'As for her, she's been the hospital's heiress since birth.'

feedback.correct_en: The gossip is describing her as the topic — commenting on her life. は sets up the topical frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify her exhaustively ('she is the one who...'), which doesn't fit the casual gossip framing.

contrast_examples.en: She is the president's daughter (pointing out among others).

prompt.context_jp: 脾臓のあたりに、見過ごせない陰影___浮かびあがっていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 見過ごせない陰影___浮かびあがっていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A shadow is newly emerging on the monitor — classic new-information が for something appearing into view.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the shadow as a known topic, but it is being discovered in this moment.

prompt.context_jp: 「医師は医師 技師___技師の役割があり」
prompt.prompt_jp: 医師は医師、技師___技師の役割があり…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the parallel contrast.

feedback.correct_en: Parallel contrastive structure: 'doctors have their role, AND technicians have theirs.' は marks the contrastive pair.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark exhaustive identification, breaking the parallel 'A-wa X, B-wa Y' contrast Omori is drawing.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は医者、母は看護師だ。
contrast_examples.en: Father is a doctor, mother is a nurse (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 「あんな小さな女の子の体に 傷___残ってしまったら…」
prompt.prompt_jp: 小さな女の子の体に 傷___残ってしまったら…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A scar coming into existence — new information in a subordinate clause with 残る. が marks the emerging subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'scar' into a contrastive topic, which doesn't fit the hypothetical 'if a scar were to remain' meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 「もし 私にもっと技術___あれば 沙里ちゃんの体に傷を残すことなく…」
prompt.prompt_jp: もし 私にもっと技術___あれば…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: ある/いる existence/possession takes が for the thing possessed: 'if I had more skill'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would add contrast ('as for skill, if I had more...'), which sounds odd here — this is a plain conditional existence.

contrast_examples.en: If I had money, I'd buy it.

prompt.context_jp: 「大きなもの___抱えてるのかもね」(甘春について)
prompt.prompt_jp: 大きなもの___抱えてるのかもね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the object of 抱えてる.

feedback.correct_en: 抱える takes a direct object marked with を: 'carrying something big (on her shoulders)'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'big thing' the subject, but 抱える is a transitive verb and the thing carried is its object.

contrast_examples.en: To have anxiety (が for ある).

prompt.context_jp: 「血管の中___進めば どの臓器にもたどりつけるという発想です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 血管の中___進めば…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 進む with a path takes を to mark the path traversed: 'advance through the blood vessels'.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an action, but with motion verbs tracing a route, を is natural.

contrast_examples.en: Play at the park (location of activity).

prompt.context_jp: 「Ｓ状結腸に こぶし大の腫瘍___あり」
prompt.prompt_jp: Ｓ状結腸に こぶし大の腫瘍___あり…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Reporting a newly observed finding on the scan — ある takes が for existence, and this is new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the tumor was already known, but Amakasu is first announcing its presence.

prompt.context_jp: 田中:「彼女1人に任せるなんて 荷が重すぎる」→五十嵐:「1人___ありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 1人___ありません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The actual line is 「1人じゃありません」— negation of 'alone' via じゃ(では)ありません. This is the natural negation form.
feedback.incorrect_en: は alone with ありません would need 一人では; '一人はありません' is ungrammatical here.

prompt.context_jp: 「患者___このまま見捨てるくらいなら 医者を名乗る意味はありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 患者___このまま見捨てるくらいなら…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 見捨てる is transitive — 'abandon the patient' takes を for the direct object.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the patient as the subject doing the abandoning, which is the opposite meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 血管造影室___、甘春が深く息を整え、モニターの前に立った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 血管造影室___、甘春が深く息を整え…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The angiography room is the location where an action (steadying her breath, standing) takes place — で marks activity location.
feedback.incorrect_en: に marks destination or existence location; で is needed because dynamic actions are performed there.

contrast_examples.en: There's a book in the room (existence).

prompt.context_jp: そこへ足音もなく五十嵐___現れ、湯呑みを片手に首を傾げた。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこへ足音もなく五十嵐___現れ…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Igarashi appears on scene — a new entrance into the narrative. 現れる with new arrivals takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark Igarashi as a continuing topic, but he's just arrived in the scene.

prompt.context_jp: 「俺たちとは 住む___違うんだからよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺たちとは 住む___違うんだからよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose what completes 'she lives in a different ___'.

feedback.correct_en: 「住む世界が違う」is a set expression meaning 'to live in a different world' — i.e., belong to a totally different class or sphere.
feedback.incorrect_en: 場所 (place) or 時代 (era) are literal and don't carry the social-sphere nuance Inou intends.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼とは住む世界が違う。
contrast_examples.en: He and I live in different worlds.

prompt.context_jp: 「だから あんなに ___目線で偉そうなんですね」
prompt.prompt_jp: あんなに ___目線で偉そうなんですね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose what fits '___ gaze' (looking down on others).

feedback.correct_en: 「上から目線」is a fixed phrase meaning a condescending/looking-down-on-you attitude.
feedback.incorrect_en: 下から目線 exists ('looking up to', obsequious) but doesn't fit 'acting high and mighty'. 横から is not a set phrase here.

contrast_examples.jp: 下から目線でお願いする。

prompt.context_jp: 「脾臓の損傷です すぐに___が必要かと」
prompt.prompt_jp: すぐに___が必要かと。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the medical term: 'immediately needs ___'.

feedback.correct_en: The spleen is bleeding, so 止血 (hemostasis / stopping the bleeding) is the needed action.
feedback.incorrect_en: 消毒 (disinfection) and 輸血 (blood transfusion) are both medical but don't address the immediate problem of ongoing bleeding from the vessel.

prompt.context_jp: 「技師が余計な___な！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 技師が余計な___な！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose what fits: 'Technician, don't butt in!'

feedback.correct_en: 「口を挟む」= to interject / butt into a conversation. Kaburaki is telling Igarashi to stop interrupting.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を貸す = lend a hand (opposite nuance); 目を離す = take one's eyes off. Neither fits the rebuke.

contrast_examples.en: Lend a hand to someone in trouble.

prompt.context_jp: 「人が___のは 自信のなさの表れだって」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人が___のは 自信のなさの表れだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose: 'People acting ___ shows a lack of confidence.'

feedback.correct_en: 威張る = to put on airs, act big/proud. The grandmother's saying is that this reveals insecurity.
feedback.incorrect_en: 謙遜する (be humble) is the opposite; 笑う (laugh) doesn't match the moralistic observation.

prompt.context_jp: 「現場の人間が リスク___ それを使わないんじゃ 意味ないじゃないですか！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 現場の人間が リスク___ それを使わないんじゃ…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb: 'if people in the field ___ risk and don't use it'.

feedback.correct_en: 恐れる = to fear. Yuki is frustrated that people avoid new tech out of fear of risk.
feedback.incorrect_en: 喜ぶ (be happy about) and 忘れる (forget) don't fit the complaint about risk-aversion.

prompt.context_jp: 「高すぎる理想は かえって自分を 追い___ことにもなる」
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分を 追い___ことにもなる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb: 'end up ___ yourself (into a corner)'.

feedback.correct_en: 追い詰める = to corner / drive someone to the wall. Omori warns that lofty ideals can corner the self.
feedback.incorrect_en: 追い抜く = overtake; 追い越す = pass/overtake. Neither matches 'drive into a corner / stress out'.

prompt.context_jp: 「鏑木先生___放射線科だと はい 私は そう感じております」
prompt.prompt_jp: 鏑木先生___放射線科だと…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'the radiology dept exists BECAUSE of Dr. Kaburagi'.

feedback.correct_en: 「NあってのN」= 'N exists only because of N'. Nokishita is sucking up: 'the department exists thanks to you.'
feedback.incorrect_en: ならでは = 'uniquely characteristic of'; にとって = 'for/to (someone)'. Neither carries the 'exists because of' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: A business depends on its customers.

prompt.context_jp: Amakasu (formal, pointing out the mess on Yuki's desk):
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for Amakasu's formal admonition?

choices.text: 昨日 あなたのデスクを 拝見しましたが ガラクタばかりで 散らかりすぎでは？
昨日 あなたのデスクを 見ちゃったけど ガラクタばっかで 汚すぎじゃん？

feedback.correct_en: Amakasu uses polite 拝見する (humble 'see') and 散らかりすぎでは？ — matching her formal, cutting tone as the director.
feedback.incorrect_en: The casual 見ちゃった/じゃん version would clash with her poised, formal persona and the workplace setting.

prompt.context_jp: Omori pressing Kaburaki about responsibility:
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is more natural for Omori's smooth, business-polite pressure?

choices.text: 院長ご自身が 責任を取られるということで よろしいでしょうか？
院長が 責任を取るってことでいいですか？

feedback.correct_en: Omori uses sonkeigo (取られる) + よろしいでしょうか to maintain polite distance while cornering Kaburaki.
feedback.incorrect_en: The plain form is too blunt for a hospital director addressing another doctor in a tense formal exchange.

contrast_examples.jp: ということでよろしいでしょうか。

prompt.context_jp: Yuki, frustrated, pushes back at the senior tech:
prompt.prompt_en: Which line matches Yuki's challenging casual tone?

choices.text: そんなこと言って ホントは 内心 ホッとしたんじゃないですか？
そのようなことを仰っておりますが 実は 安堵されたのではないでしょうか？

feedback.correct_en: Among coworkers, Yuki uses semi-polite but pointed ホントは… ホッとしたんじゃないですか — natural confrontation among colleagues.
feedback.incorrect_en: The ultra-formal 仰る/安堵/のではないでしょうか sounds absurdly stiff between techs in the break room.

contrast_examples.jp: ホッとしたんじゃないですか？
安堵されたのではないでしょうか。
contrast_examples.en: Have you not been relieved? (overly formal)

prompt.context_jp: Inou reassuring the patient's family about the radiology team:
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for a confident, reassuring staff reply?

choices.text: 当院一優秀な放射線科チームが 最善の治療を 提供するわけですから 安心して お待ちください
うちで一番すごい放射線のチームが めっちゃいい治療をするから 心配しないで待ってて

feedback.correct_en: Addressing a worried family in a hospital, Inou uses 当院/最善/提供する/お待ちください — the expected polished register.
feedback.incorrect_en: めっちゃ/すごい/待ってて is far too casual for a staff member reassuring anxious family members.

contrast_examples.jp: 最善の治療を提供いたします。
contrast_examples.en: We will provide the best treatment.

contrast_examples.jp: めっちゃいい治療するよ。
contrast_examples.en: We'll do a really great treatment (too casual).
